related_questions.question: What disqualifies you from Social Security?

text_blocks.snippet: Several factors can disqualify an individual from receiving Social Security benefits. These include not having enough work credits, being under the full retirement age and earning too much, certain criminal activity like violating parole or committing fraud, and failure to cooperate with the Social Security Administration (SSA) such as not attending required medical exams or providing necessary information. Additionally, some countries of residence may disqualify individuals from receiving benefits while living abroad.
snippet_highlighted_words: not having enough work credits, being under the full retirement age and earning too much, certain criminal activity like violating parole or committing fraud, and failure to cooperate with the Social Security Administration (SSA) such as not attending required medical exams or providing necessary information

list.title: Insufficient Work Credits:
list.snippet: To qualify for retirement benefits, individuals generally need 40 Social Security credits, which are earned through covered earnings.

list.title: Earnings Above the Limit:
list.snippet: If an individual is under the full retirement age and earns above a certain amount, their benefits may be reduced or suspended, according to the Social Security Administration (.gov).

list.title: Disability Not Meeting SSA Definition:
list.snippet: For disability benefits, the SSA requires that the impairment be expected to last at least 12 months or result in death, and that it prevents the individual from performing any substantial gainful activity.

list.title: Failure to Cooperate:
list.snippet: Failing to attend scheduled medical exams, provide requested information, or adhere to treatment plans can lead to denial or suspension of benefits.

list.title: Criminal Activity:
list.snippet: Violating parole or probation conditions, or being convicted of fraud related to Social Security benefits, can lead to disqualification.

list.title: Residency in Certain Countries:
list.snippet: Some countries are not eligible for Social Security benefits to be sent to, even if the individual has otherwise qualified.

list.title: Committing Fraud:
list.snippet: If an individual is found to have obtained benefits through fraudulent means, they can be disqualified and potentially prosecuted.

list.title: Early Retirement:
list.snippet: Claiming benefits before the full retirement age results in a reduced benefit amount.

list.title: Taxes:
list.snippet: While not a disqualification, a portion of Social Security benefits may be subject to federal income tax, which could reduce the amount received.
